correctness.rationale: Poisson Fourier convolution gives exact scalar objective. A global O(r) localization bound plus negative Hessian proves unique bisector fit at small r. An explicit \(1/(1-r)\) witness, denominator control, a compact scaled limit with unique strict maximum, and an implicit-function argument yield exactly two high-r global fits. Exact derivative expansion proves the inward fourth-order shift; exact \(L^2\) norm gives the universal positive error coefficient. 99 deterministic finite diagnostics replay; none is substituted for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Best-one-kernel compression of a separated pair of Poisson harmonic measures is a canonical resolution and approximation question. The two-to-one optimizer transition, universal high-concentration fitted scale, nonzero fourth-order inward drift and unavoidable sharp \(1/(1-r)\) squared-error cost constitute a structural phenomenon not implied by co-centered or antipodal special cases. Intermediate threshold uniqueness is not claimed.
